run_metadata.coverage_summary: Degraded, SEARCH-ONLY run (2026-11-22). The hard outbound-network block seen on recent runs persists and was re-tested at the start of this run: WebFetch to https://www.tenders.gov.au/atm, https://www.tenders.act.gov.au/tenders/open and https://www.vendorpanel.com.au/publictenders.aspx all returned DNS ENOTFOUND (host outside the session's allowed network domains). No buyer-originated detail page, RSS/JSON feed, API endpoint, or tender document could be opened this run. Discovery was therefore limited to WebSearch, which is US-indexed and lagging the 2026-11-22 run date, returning mostly cached snapshots, buyer-page snapshots, trade press, and third-party aggregator pages. Tier 1 swept by search (AusTender/Defence; NSW buy.nsw/eTendering; VIC Buying for Victoria; QLD QTenders->VendorPanel/supply.qld.gov.au; WA Tenders WA + regional development-commission bulletins; SA Tenders SA; TAS Tenders Tasmania/Business Tasmania; NT QTOL; ACT Tenders). Tier 2 swept by search (councils on VendorPanel/eTenderBox/TenderLink; GBEs incl. Sydney Water, Melbourne Water, NBN Co, Transgrid; universities; CSIRO). Tier 3 MANDATORY check done by search (SAP Business Network / Ariba Discovery, BHP GCMS, Rio Tinto Ariba, EstimateOne, Coupa) - every corporate channel remained registration-gated or invitation-only with no publicly-visible open RFx this run; all are already in the known-source set, none fabricated. Net result: ONE genuinely new buyer-originated opportunity captured at headline level - the Western Australia Service Alliance 2012 (SA12) regional building-maintenance registration arrangement (Dept of Housing and Works), whose November 2026 invitation PDF is publicly published on wa.gov.au - recorded as both a new tender and a new source. All other search hits were already in the baseline, had closed, or were aggregator-only (do-not-rely) listings and were not re-captured.
gaps: HARD EGRESS BLOCK (unchanged from recent runs): WebFetch to all external hosts fails with DNS ENOTFOUND - confirmed this run for www.tenders.gov.au, www.tenders.act.gov.au, www.vendorpanel.com.au and www.developmentaid.org. No buyer portal, feed, API or tender document could be directly opened. These hosts must be added to the session's allowed network domains for a full-fidelity run. Until then every run is search-only and detail extraction from tender documents is impossible.
Tier 1 Commonwealth (AusTender): could not open https://www.tenders.gov.au/atm; no live ATM list retrievable; search returned only cached/stale ATM snapshots and aggregator pages. Deferred.

Tier 1 NSW (buy.nsw/eTendering): opportunities hub not fetchable; only the already-known ~$80M Master Media RFT (closing 27 Nov) surfaced, plus platform guidance. Deferred to a future authenticated/allowed run.

Tier 1 VIC (tenders.vic.gov.au): portal is JavaScript-rendered; search returned only cached 'open/future/closed' pages whose listings had already closed (Oct 2026). No current Nov-2026 VIC tender confirmable.
Tier 1 QLD (QTenders -> VendorPanel/supply.qld.gov.au): mid-migration; no live list fetchable; aggregator (qld2032) listings stale/closed. Deferred.
Tier 1 WA/SA/TAS/NT/ACT: portals not fetchable; only cached/closed listings or weekly-roundup PDFs surfaced.

Tier 2 GBEs (Sydney Water, Melbourne Water, NBN Co, Transgrid, etc.): current-tenders pages not fetchable; search returned mostly closed notices and infrastructure-pipeline briefings (forward-looking milestones, not open RFx).

Tier 3 corporate (SAP Ariba Discovery, BHP GCMS, Rio Tinto Ariba, EstimateOne, Coupa): all registration-gated or invitation-only; no publicly-visible open RFx; recorded as portals (already in known-source set), none fabricated.

Aggregator-only hits (australiantenders.com.au, biddetail, tendersontime, globaltenders, developmentaid, qld2032) were used only as discovery signals and NOT captured as opportunities, per the buyer-originated-only rule; none were paywall-confirmable against a buyer source this run.
recommended_seed_additions: Department of Housing and Works (WA) - Service Alliance 2012 (SA12) regional building-maintenance registration arrangement (wa.gov.au/government/publications/service-alliance-2012-invitation) - open rolling prequalification for regional WA contractors; worth adding to the permanent known-source list and re-checking monthly for refreshed invitations.

ALLOW-LIST REQUEST (infrastructure, not a tender source): add the Tier-1 portal hosts (tenders.gov.au, tenders.nsw.gov.au, tenders.vic.gov.au, qtenders.hpw.qld.gov.au, supply.qld.gov.au, tenders.wa.gov.au, tenders.sa.gov.au, tenders.tas.gov.au, tendersonline.nt.gov.au, tenders.act.gov.au) plus vendorpanel.com.au to the session network policy so future runs can fetch live detail pages and feeds.

tenders.source_name: Department of Housing and Works (WA) - Service Alliance 2012 (SA12)
tenders.title: Service Alliance 2012 (SA12) - Invitation to register for regional building maintenance and improvement works
tenders.buyer: Department of Housing and Works (WA) - Buildings and Contracts, Regional Operations Division
tenders.description: Standing 'Service Alliance 2012' (SA12) arrangement under which locally based regional Western Australian contractors can register to be eligible for government building-related maintenance and improvement work. A refreshed invitation to register was published on wa.gov.au dated 5 November 2026. Registration is open on a rolling basis; it is an expression of interest to perform services and does not guarantee any work.
tenders.deliverables_summary: Successful applicants join the SA12 arrangement and become eligible to be engaged for building-related maintenance and improvement works valued up to $250,000 across regional Western Australia, delivered for the Department of Housing and Works (and, from 1 July 2026, extending to Department of Communities sites per the department's maintenance bulletin). Scope is general building repairs, maintenance and minor improvement works using locally based contractors.
tenders.scope_of_work: Building-related maintenance and improvement works up to $250,000 in value for government agency buildings in regional WA, delivered through the Service Alliance 2012 (SA12) contractual arrangement administered by the Department of Housing and Works' Buildings and Contracts, Regional Operations Division.
requirements: Be a locally based contractor operating in the relevant regional WA area
Complete the SA12 pre-application form and accept the Service Alliance 2012 conditions of contract
tenders.eligibility: Open arrangement - locally based regional WA contractors may apply for membership at any time; registration is an expression of interest and does not guarantee the award of any work.
tenders.submission_method: Complete the SA12 pre-application form and submit to the Department of Housing and Works per the invitation document (open/rolling registration).
mandatory_conditions: Acceptance of the Service Alliance 2012 general conditions of contract
tenders.detail_source: WebSearch index snapshot of the buyer's own invitation document at https://www.wa.gov.au/system/files/2026-11/service-alliance-2012-invitation-05112026.pdf (dated 5 Nov 2026) and related SA12 publications on wa.gov.au. The PDF itself could not be opened directly this run due to the egress block.
tenders.reasoning: Discovered via WebSearch for recent WA tender/registration activity; the search surfaced the buyer-originated invitation PDF on wa.gov.au dated 05112026. Captured from the buying organisation's own publication (not an aggregator). Buyer = Department of Housing and Works (WA).
tenders.notes: Headline-level capture only - counted in entries_pending_detail. The full invitation PDF and conditions-of-contract document could not be fetched this run (hard egress block: DNS ENOTFOUND on all external hosts), so key_deliverables, evaluation_criteria, precise contract term, delivery regions and contacts remain unverified and are left empty/null rather than inferred. This is an open, rolling prequalification arrangement with no fixed closing date (closing_date null by design). Value '$250,000' is the per-engagement eligibility ceiling stated in the SA12 scope, not a single contract value. A future run with portal access should open the invitation PDF to extract the full scope, regional lots, insurance/licence conditions and contacts.
